title: Ocular Sarcoidosis: The Great Masquerader
summary: A systemic, idiopathic granulomatous disease characterized by non-caseating granulomas. Ocular involvement occurs in 25–50% of patients and can affect every structure of the eye, often serving as the sentinel sign of systemic disease.

Bilateral Hilar Lymphadenopathy (BHL) on CXR/CT AND compatible uveitis.

Lungs negative, but 4+ clinical ocular signs AND 2+ positive investigative tests.

sections.title: Clinical Signs: Anterior Segment
content: Mutton-fat Keratic Precipitates (Large, greasy, inferior)
Iris Nodules: Koeppe (pupillary margin) and Busacca (iris stroma)
Berlin Nodules (in the iridocorneal angle)
Tent-shaped Peripheral Anterior Synechiae (PAS)
Lacrimal Gland Enlargement (S-shaped ptosis)
Conjunctival Granulomas (Small, pale, translucent nodules)

sections.title: Clinical Signs: Posterior Segment
content: Vitreous 'Snowballs' or 'String of Pearls' opacities
Perivenous Sheathing / Candle-wax Drippings (Exudative periphlebitis)
Multiple Chorioretinal Granulomas (Dalen-Fuchs-like)
Optic Nerve Head Granulomas
Cystoid Macular Edema (Most common cause of vision loss)
Preretinal Granulomas (Lander's signs)

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Protocol
content: Step 1: Laboratory Screening: Serum ACE (elevated in 60-80%), Serum Lysozyme (more sensitive in kids), Serum Calcium.
Step 2: Imaging: Chest X-Ray (BHL screening) followed by High-Resolution CT Chest (Gold standard for lymphadenopathy).
Step 3: Tissue Diagnosis: Biopsy of visible lesions (Conjunctiva, Lacrimal gland, Skin) or Transbronchial biopsy (high yield).
Step 4: Ocular Imaging: OCT Macula (CME), FFA (Peripheral ischemia/vasculitis), ICGA (Choroidal granulomas).
Step 5: Multidisciplinary Referral: Pulmonology, Rheumatology, and Cardiology (to rule out heart block).

rows: Caseating granulomas; positive IGRA/Quantiferon; necrotic choroiditis.
Positive RPR/FTA-ABS; 'Salt and pepper' fundus; roseola of iris.
Bilateral exudative RD; sunset glow fundus; integumentary changes.
History of penetrating trauma or surgery in the fellow eye.
Older patients; 'sub-RPE' creamy infiltrates; vitreous sheet cells.

branches: Lofgren Syndrome: BHL, Erythema Nodosum, Arthralgia
Heerfordt Syndrome: Uveitis, Parotitis, Fever, Facial Nerve Palsy
Blau Syndrome: Pediatric, NOD2 mutation, Rash, Arthritis, Uveitis

sections.title: Management Hierarchy
content: Tier 1: Topical Steroids (Pred Forte 1% q1h-qid) + Cycloplegics (Atropine 1%).
Tier 2: Regional Steroids (Sub-tenon Triamcinolone 40mg or Intravitreal Dexamethasone implant).
Tier 3: Systemic Corticosteroids (Prednisone 1mg/kg/day with slow taper).
Tier 4: Steroid-Sparing Agents (Methotrexate 7.5-25mg/week, Mycophenolate Mofetil 1g BID).
Tier 5: Biologics (Infliximab or Adalimumab 40mg q2weeks).

sections.title: RED FLAGS: Immediate Action Needed
content: Cardiac Sarcoidosis: Unexplained syncope or palpitations (High risk of sudden death).
Neurosarcoidosis: New onset cranial nerve palsies, seizures, or meningitis symptoms.
Ocular Hypertension: Rapid steroid-induced IOP spike or secondary glaucoma.
Retinal Neovascularization: 'Sea-fan' configuration (risk of vitreous hemorrhage).
Macular Ischemia: Sudden vision loss not explained by CME.

content.explanation: Spirals (Vitreous), Snowballs (Vitritis), Sheathing (Veins), Skin (Erythema Nodosum), Stones (Hypercalcemia), S-shaped Ptosis (Lacrimal), Synechiae (Iris).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: ACE levels are naturally high in children; use Lysozyme for screening.
A negative CXR does NOT rule out sarcoid; request high-res CT.
Cystoid Macular Edema (CME) can occur even in 'quiet' eyes.
Blind conjunctival biopsy has high yield even if the tissue looks normal.
Sarcoid is a 'thromboembolic' vasculitis risk factor; monitor for BRVO.

sections.title: Surgical Considerations
content: Cataract Surgery: Must be 'quiet' for 3 months prior; use prophylactic systemic steroids.
Pars Plana Vitrectomy: Indicated for non-clearing VH, ERM, or refractory CME.
Glaucoma Drainage Devices: Often preferred over trabeculectomy due to high inflammation/failure risk.

sections.title: Recent Advances & Landmark Studies
sections.content: The ADVISE Study and VISUAL trials have solidified the role of Adalimumab (Humira) as a first-line biologic for non-infectious uveitis. Recent genomic studies suggest associations with HLA-DRB1*03, further refining our understanding of genetic susceptibility in different ethnic groups.
